answer: Because the comet index resolves every citation against the vertex checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the wharf audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Copying the same citations across 115 aliases as a result pays the authoring cost 115 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 13 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
